data.name: Aijaz
data.gender_notes: Aijaz is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root "a-j-z". It means to support, strengthen, and be a pillar. In Islamic history, Aijaz was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) known for his unwavering faith and support. The name Aijaz carries the meaning “Strong support” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aijaz usually hope their child will grow to embody strong support and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the wisdom and intelligence bestowed upon us by Allah. It encourages the bearer to seek knowledge, grow spiritually, and use their intellect to serve others and make a positive impact on the world.
data.etymology: Aijaz belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Strong support.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aijaz total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Aijaz carries a rich cultural significance in Arabic and Islamic heritage. It signifies a person who is strong, resilient, and offers support to those around them. In many cultures and societies, the name has been passed down through generations, emphasizing the importance of strength, unity, and solidarity.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper level, the name Aijaz holds great spiritual significance for Muslims. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) had a close companion named Aijaz ibn Kulfah, who was known for his unwavering faith and devotion to Islam. Aijaz is an inspiration for Muslims today, reminding us of the importance of unwavering faith, patience, and loyalty. It serves as a reminder that, like Aijaz, we too can be pillars of support and strength for our families, communities, and faith.
